sources.name: 23 Most Gay Friendly Cities in the US - Insider Monkey
These are the 15 most LGBTQ-friendly cities in the U.S + Advocate

_: Los Angeles is a tolerant city. Just 15 percent opposed non-discrimination laws, which was 21 percent less than the national average at the time of the study.
Chicago had a state equality tally score of 37.5 at the time of the study, a remarkable 125 percent above the state average.
San Diego has 0.12 pride events per 100,000 residents annually which was 71 percent above the average in the study.
Just behind Richmond, the Silicon Valley city of San Jose has a municipal equality score of 97 out of 100.
San Francisco ranks near the top of almost every category, making it the most LGBTQ-friendly city in the U.S.
Denver had an equality score 154 percent higher than average, as well as 25 percent more LGBTQ-affirming healthcare providers per 100,000 residents than the average metro area in the study.
The Las Vegas metro area has 0.22 pride events per 100,000 residents annually, a staggering 214 percent more than the average metro area in the study.
Maryland has a state equality score 89 percent higher than others in the study.
The Milwaukee metro area has 0.45 gay bars per 100,000 residents, which is 50 percent more than the average city in the study
Like Richmond, the capital city of California earned a perfect municipal score.
New Orleans had 1.43 gay bars per 100,000 residents, which is the highest in the study.
Pittsburg offers 2.72 LGBTQ-affirming healthcare providers per 100,000 residents, which is 94 higher than the average metro in the study.
Richmond boasts a perfect municipal equality score of 100 in the study.
Hartford is the third-smallest metro area in the study, but only 11 percent of residents oppose marriage equality, the lowest in the study.
